column2: The selected chapter starts at verse 2. Incense at high places is explained by no house yet built for the Lord's name; absent verse 1 is not reconstructed.
Solomon's love and walking in David's ordinances remain alongside the however qualification about high-place sacrifices and incense.
Gibeon's highest and great description retains the superlative rather than simply important; one thousand whole burnt offerings and the repeated location remain.
column3: The precise referent of the feminine description and its topographical or cultic force remain provisional.

column2: Propose Make a request for yourself as natural English for the cognate ask-a-request imperative. Appearance in sleep at night and the repeated Lord/Solomon names remain.
Direct divine address uses Thou, Thy and Thee, preserving mercy, truth, righteousness, upright heart, the kept mercy and the son seated this day.
Lord my God, the servant's placement instead of David, little child and ignorance of going out/coming in remain without substituting a particular administrative skill.
The chosen people, servant among them and uncountable multitude retain the election and number clauses in direct divine address.
The hearing heart, righteous judgment, good/evil distinction and weighty people retain the request's successive purposes.
column3: Give interprets the future doseis as a petition in context; weighty does not settle whether the people are numerous, burdensome or formidable.

column2: The Lord's pleasure is tied to Solomon asking this particular thing, without a broader approval of every action.
The divine reply uses ordinary you to Solomon; repeated negatives distinguish many days, wealth and enemies' lives from understanding to hear judgment.
Both beholds, accomplished gift, discerning and wise heart, no earlier equal and no future equal retain the selected sequence and temporal scope.
Unasked wealth and glory are also given; no equal has been among kings remains past, with no imported lifetime limitation.
If retains the condition for multiplied days: walking God's way and keeping both commands and ordinances as David did.
Propose behold at the dream recognition. The selected altar before the covenant ark in Zion, both offering types and feast for king and attendants remain.
column3: Great feast renders the drinking-banquet term potos broadly; no abstinence or specific drink is implied. The source's present-tense arrival is narrated in ordinary English past sequence.

column2: Both women are identified as prostitutes and appear and stand before the king; no other occupation or moral commentary replaces the designation.
Please realizes the entreaty idiom; the women share one house and both gave birth there, with no added witness.
The third-day interval and only the two women in the house retain the asserted chronology and absence of others.
The other child's nighttime death from the mother's lying on him remains the first woman's testimony, not an independently narrated reconstruction.
Midnight rising, removal from the speaker's arms and the two bosom placements preserve the alleged exchange and each child's identity.
Propose both selected beholds around the morning examination and recognition. Nursing, the child's death and denial that he is her own remain.
The other woman's denial and living/dead opposition retain the shorter selected speech; an additional rebuttal is not imported before the collective speech summary.
The king repeats both claims, their direct address and living/dead distinctions; repetition is not condensed into a summary dispute.
The request for a sword and its presentation are preserved as separate narrated actions; execution is not yet said to occur.
The living nursing child, division in two and a half for each woman retain the king's exact stated test without endorsing it as a general instruction.
The narrator identifies the living child's mother and her stirred womb; her plea against death contrasts with the other's neither-me-nor-her demand.
column3: The other supplies the contextual subject of the second this-one pronoun; the womb image is not reduced to a purely intellectual decision.

column2: Propose extending the inner quotation through the prohibition of death, so the identifying words match the mother's full plea in verse 26. Giving the child and she is his mother remain.
column3: Quotation boundaries are editorial; the selected Greek has no modern quotation marks. This choice identifies both repeated clauses as her words without changing their content.

column2: All Israel hears, fears the king and recognizes divine discernment for doing justice; no attribution of omniscience is added.
The administrative chapter opens with Solomon reigning over Israel; all Israel is not added where this unit lacks all.
Azariah son of Zadok opens the officials list without an imported priest title.
Elihoreph and Ahijah son of Saba are scribes, followed by Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud as recorder.
column3: The singular son attachment is retained with Ahijah; shared parentage for both scribes is not silently asserted.

column2: Both Zadok and Abiathar are called priests despite Abiathar's earlier removal; no chronological reconciliation is inserted.
Ornia supervises appointed officers and Zabud is the king's companion, retaining names and roles distinct from the chapter 2 list.
Achiel's stewardship, Eliab son of Saph over the clan and Adoniram son of Ephra over tributes remain as selected.
column3: Clan and tributes are provisional administrative equivalents; forced labor or a particular tribal structure is not silently substituted.

column2: Twelve officers provision king and household, each for one month per year, preserving count, recipients and rotation.
Benor in Ephraim's hill country retains the explicit one and the selected name rather than dividing it into a familiar patronymic.
The son of Rechab and all five geographical expressions remain in order, including the as-far-as boundary and one.
The son of Esoth and Berbethnema, Lousamencha and Rhesphara remain; no absent one is appended.
column3: Place/name segmentation and the supplied in remain provisional; familiar Hebrew locations are not substituted.

column2: Chinanadab, Anaphathi, husband of Tableth, Solomon's daughter as wife and one all remain visible in the difficult sequence.
column3: The grammatical division between names, location and marital clause remains unresolved. This wording does not establish two distinct officials or normalize the line to Ben-abinadab in Dor.

column2: Baccha son of Ahilud, Taanach, Megiddo, house of San and the full boundary chain through Maeber Loukam remain, with one.
column3: Exact geography and several name divisions remain provisional; supplied over expresses the list's implied administrative relation.

column2: Geber's son at Remath-gilead receives Eregaba's district in Bashan with sixty large walled cities and bronze bars, retaining one and omitting no listed feature.
Ahinadab son of Achel, Mahanaim and one remain without replacing the selected father name.
Ahimaaz at Naphtali, also marrying Solomon's daughter Basemath, and one preserve the second marriage notice.
Baana son of Hushai at Maalath remains with one; no pair of familiar tribal territories replaces Maalath.
Shammah son of Elah in Benjamin remains, without an added one where absent.
Geber son of Adai, Gad's land, both Sihon and Og with their kingdoms, and one officer in Judah remain in the selected order.
column3: Officer interprets the transliterated nasiph; the exact office is provisional. Judah is not replaced by a statement that he alone governed all the preceding land.

column2: Jehoshaphat son of Phouasoud in Issachar closes the selected list; the entry is not relocated to match another ordering.
